questions.q:
Which of the following phrases given below the sentence should replace the phrase given in bold to make the sentence grammatically correct? Choose the best option among the four given alternatives that reflects the correct phrase to be used in the sentence.

I had to use trials and errors to figure out how to fix my car.
questions.s: There are several phrases in English where two or more nouns are used together as a single noun and treated as singular. For example, bread and butter, black and white etc. 'Trial and error' is one such phrase, which refers to a process of solving a problem through repeated attempts and mistakes. So, the phrase in bold needs to be replaced by 'trial and error'. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q:
In the question given below, one part of the sentence may or may not have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

You need to(A)/ constantly target(B)/ your bicep by(C)/ using a curl rod(D).
questions.s:
Part C has an error. Some nouns are used only in the plural forms. Some examples are: jeans, trousers, pants, tights, shorts, pyjamas, scissors, etc. 'Biceps' is one such word. So, 'bicep' needs to be replaced by 'biceps' in the given sentence in order to rectify the error. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence would be: You need to constantly target your biceps using a curl rod.

questions.q: In the classroom, students sat at their desks, rows upon rows, listening to the teacher's instructions.
questions.s:
When a preposition comes after a noun and then the same noun is repeated, the noun should be used in singular form. Therefore, “row upon row” should come in place of “rows upon rows”.

So, the correct sentence would be: “In the classroom, students sat at their desks, row upon row, listening to the teacher's instructions.”

questions.q:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Policeman came to my village and asked about a person who burgled a house last night.
questions.s:
The error is in the word "policeman," which is a singular noun without an article. In English, singular countable nouns typically require an article ("a," "an," or "the") unless they are proper nouns or used in a general sense.

In this sentence, "Policeman" refers to a specific individual who came to the village, so it should be "The policeman" or "A policeman." The absence of an article makes the sentence grammatically incorrect. Thus, the option "policeman" contains the error.

The correct sentence is-" A/The policeman came to my village and asked about a person who burgled a house last night."
